standard_prerequisites.name: The three formulations of being an equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is a half adjoint equivalence when it has a quasi-inverse with a coherence, and bi-invertible when it has a separate left and right inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two types compared by the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Implications between the formulations
standard_prerequisites.statement: A bi-invertible map is a quasi-inverse map, a quasi-inverse map is a half adjoint equivalence, and each of these steps is also available in the reverse direction.
standard_prerequisites.use: They provide the two maps of the equivalence, one for each direction of the chain in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Both formulations are mere propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: Being a half adjoint equivalence and being bi-invertible are both mere propositions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows the two implications to be upgraded to an equivalence by the cited criterion.

core_obligations: Give one map of the equivalence by composing the implication from bi-invertible maps to quasi-inverse maps with the implication from quasi-inverse maps to half adjoint equivalences (source line 409).
Give the map in the other direction by composing the reverse implications, from half adjoint equivalences to quasi-inverse maps and from there to bi-invertible maps (source line 409).
Upgrade the two implications to an equivalence, which is legitimate because both types are mere propositions, by the cited criterion for propositions (source line 410).

proof_roadmap.step: The two maps of the equivalence, one for each direction of the chain of implications.
Both types are mere propositions, so the criterion upgrades the maps to an equivalence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled corollary at source lines 405-407: the bi-invertible maps are equivalent to the half adjoint equivalences. The proof (source lines 408-411) is short but it supplies both maps of the equivalence explicitly, by composing the two chains of implications between the formulations of being an equivalence, and then observes that the goal may be closed by the criterion for mere propositions because both types are mere propositions. Choosing the two composites and seeing which hypothesis upgrades them to an equivalence is the substance, and the statement alone shows none of it.
